Does NOT shut down the shared AACommServer process — call CloseAACommServer(bool) for that. public void Dispose() DownloadArray(string, int, IReadOnlyList, bool, int, bool) Downloads contiguous floating-point array values and blocks for one final result. Ethernet only: on any other channel type it throws NotSupportedException. Uses Zynq stream transport when advertised by both peers; otherwise uses legacy bulk messages, or one message per element for a parameter not allowed in bulk. A timeout or disconnect is never retried because part of the array may already have been applied. Every element is checked against the controller's message table first: one whose index or value the table rules out ends the call as Rejected with that element's index and error code, and nothing is sent. A parameter the table refuses outright (unknown, read-only, not an array) throws ArgumentException. public ArrayDownloadResult DownloadArray(string parameter, int firstIndex, IReadOnlyList values, bool continueOnError = false, int timeoutMs = 60000, bool skipUserUnits = false) Parameters parameter string Axis-qualified array parameter without an index, for example BPVAJList. firstIndex int One-based array index receiving values[0]. values IReadOnlyList Contiguous values to download. continueOnError bool Continue applying values after a controller error. timeoutMs int Budget for each request and reply. The server arms the same budget against the controller and tears the channel down as fatal when it expires, so a stalled download also stalls whatever is queued behind it for every client on that channel. skipUserUnits bool Bypass User Units conversion for this download. Returns ArrayDownloadResult Remarks On ProtocolError with CrcMismatch the controller verifies the payload checksum only after applying every element, so the result reports a full AppliedCount for a write whose integrity check failed. Read the array back rather than trusting that count. Wire format: Firmware-Main docs/features/Array-Stream-Download.md. Note: in case connectionData.CommChannelType == RS_232, Identity[22] => RS232 cable type is also queried, and is updated public ConnectResult TestConnection(ConnectionData connectionData, bool isKnownControllerType) Parameters connectionData ConnectionData the required connection data isKnownControllerType bool set to FALSE, if testing connection vs. an unknown controller Returns ConnectResult ConnectResult Events OnCommsError Fatal communication error. If AACommServer was closed unexpectedly the string is AACommServerNotRunning. Suppressed only when a SendReceive(AACommMessage) was in flight AND no concurrent async Send(AACommMessage) was in flight (sync caller observes via the SR return; mixed-mode fatals still fire). Invoked synchronously on the transport receiver thread — off-load long work via Task.Run. Do NOT call API functions from the handler; no Disconnect needed after. Also raised when a SendReceive(AACommMessage) timeout closes the connection, on that caller's thread before it returns. public event Action OnCommsError Event Type Action OnLongOperationEnded Fired when a long controller operation (Reset, Save, Load, SaveUser, EventCorrect) ends. Parameters: identifying the operation, and the controller error code — 0 means no error (the operation succeeded); a non-zero value is the controller error code (e.g. 22 = "motor on"), or an unresolved-error sentinel when the operation ended without a parseable reply (e.g. session teardown). Fired only if the matching fired: a long op whose reply lands within the start-grace window raises neither edge (see ). Do NOT call API functions while handling. Event is invoked in a new Task. Event NOT invoked if method is used. For Reset: NOT invoked if the Reset reply was an error, if reconnecting after reset failed, or if the API was disconnected while in reset progress. public event Action OnLongOperationEnded Event Type Action OnLongOperationStarted Fired when a long controller operation (Reset, Save, Load, SaveUser, EventCorrect) begins. Parameter: identifying the operation. For Save/Load/SaveUser/EventCorrect: NOT fired when the controller replies within a short start-grace window — such a reply means the op was not long-running (e.g. an immediate ERR 22 rejecting a flash Save while the motor is on), and the reply surfaces its own result; the matching is suppressed too. Do NOT call API functions while handling. Event is invoked in a new Task. Event NOT invoked if method is used. public event Action OnLongOperationStarted Event Type Action OnPushMessageReceived Raised when an unsolicited "push" message is received from the controller. The event delivers a parsed AACommPushMsgBase instance (created by AACommPushMsgBase.Parse) and is invoked on a background Task to avoid blocking the receiver thread. Handlers should be aware that multiple push messages may be received in quick succession, so code re-entry and thread-safety should be considered. public event Action OnPushMessageReceived Event Type Action OnUserUnitsEnabledChanged Raised after the controller confirms (OK reply) a per-axis User Units enable/disable change, regardless of the path that sent it (API, Terminal, …). Fires only on an actual transition. The cache behind GetUserUnitsEnabled(char) is updated synchronously on the receiver thread before this fires, so handlers should re-read it rather than rely on event ordering. Invoked on a background Task (like OnPushMessageReceived); consider re-entrancy and thread-safety. Args: (axis, isEnabled). public event Action OnUserUnitsEnabledChanged Event Type Action

AcquisitionSource The transport or protocol path, and the name of what was read. Attempt One run of one operation. Observations, evidence and restore steps link to it. Capture When a value was captured, in the clock named by Domain. CommissioningIssue CommissioningKeys Quantity keys the validator knows the shape of. CommissioningReport A versioned record of what a commissioning or discovery pass observed. It states what each value means and how it was obtained; it does not establish physical identity, loaded bytes, permission to actuate or hardware qualification. CommissioningValidation Outcome of Validate(CommissioningReport). A clean result says the report agrees with itself; it says nothing about the rig. CommissioningValidator Checks a CommissioningReport for internal contradictions. Declaration An expected artifact or source, kept apart from anything observed at runtime. EvidenceRef A file held outside the report. The report never infers that it exists. Limit A limit an attempt declared before acting. Observation One value, or the explicit absence of one, obtained by one attempt. ObservationValue A scalar. Exactly one member is set. Integer is a signed 64-bit value kept exactly; Real must be finite. A quantity that is an exact count is an Integer. PassiveCollectionRequest What to collect: caller-supplied ids and the port/axis/encoder links to read through. PassiveEncoderSelection Opts one request mapping's scope into passive absolute-encoder metadata collection. PassiveKeys Quantity keys the passive collector records, beside CommissioningKeys. PassiveMetadataCollector Reads metadata the shared AAComm interfaces already expose into a CommissioningReport, with ordinary parameter reads only: no setting write, protocol query, recorder arm, motor enable, Save or reset. RestoreStep A step that puts a changed setting or the motor state back, with its readback. Scope Where a value applies. api/AAComm.Extensions.AACommDownloadFPGA.summary: Class AACommDownloadFPGARemote Namespace AAComm.Extensions Assembly AAComm.dll Asynchronous service class used for downloading FPGA to AGM400 and AGM800 products Remote Unit Make sure to set the correct <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.AACommRemoteFpgaInfo.Port" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.AACommRemoteFpgaInfo.AllowForce" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (if need) When starting the DL process, the API state must be NOT connected. Process ends with API state: Disconnected (success or error) Remote image transitions require checked preparation, reconnect and fresh dual-configuration state: boot (3/4) before flash writes, primary (2/5) before success. Only ERR 151 on the final reconfiguration trigger may proceed to that verification; it is reported through <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.AACommDownloadFPGARemote.OnStatus" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> as uncertain completion. Other failures terminate without retrying erase or image transfer. Process can't be canceled in the middle. public class AACommDownloadFPGARemote Inheritance object AACommDownloadFPGARemote Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties OnProcessEnded indicated the end of the Remote FPGA DL process. String parameters indicates status. Empty for success, error description otherwise. Also invoked, with an error description, for a refused call; a refusal raised before this call connects disconnects no <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>, a failure after its own <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.Connect(AAComm.Services.ConnectionData%2cSystem.Boolean)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> succeeded closes only the connection it opened, and neither ends a download already running on this instance. In case "Force" is set to "false", but force may be needed, an appropriate error is reported. See <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.AACommRemoteFpgaInfo.AllowForce" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> for "Force" download options! public Action<string> OnProcessEnded { get; set; } Property Value Action<string> OnProgress reports the binary data download progress, 0 to 100 public Action<int> OnProgress { get; set; } Property Value Action<int> OnStatus reports the current status of Remote FPGA DL process as string public Action<string> OnStatus { get; set; } Property Value Action<string> Methods StartDownloading(CommAPI, ConnectionData, AACommRemoteFpgaInfo) asynchronous function, starts downloading Remote FPGA Make sure to set the correct <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.AACommRemoteFpgaInfo.Port" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.AACommRemoteFpgaInfo.AllowForce" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (if need) the API object must be NOT connected! Identity/file checks are required before either image transition. A successful reconnect or cached identity does not verify the requested image; failed verification ends the download with an error. public void StartDownloading(CommAPI api, ConnectionData connData, AACommRemoteFpgaInfo fpgaInfo) Parameters api CommAPI instance of the API class to perform the download connData ConnectionData connection data fpgaInfo AACommRemoteFpgaInfo remote FPGA data/version container, see AACommRemoteFpgaInfo for details! Its RPD image must be a non-empty whole number of 4-byte words; any other length is refused before connecting

String parameters indicates status. Empty for success, error description otherwise. Also invoked, with an error description, for a refused call; a refusal raised before this call connects disconnects no , a failure after its own succeeded closes only the connection it opened, and neither ends a download already running on this instance. public Action OnProcessEnded { get; set; } Property Value Action OnProgress reports the binary data download progress, in fractions of 1000(!) Additional safety checks are performed prior to downloading FW, and

'Verify Currents' requires: HEX file with identity data, NOT AGM800 family, controller NOT in BOOT mode public void StartDownloadingSafe(CommAPI api, ConnectionData connData, string fwDataFile, string verFile, string password, bool verifyCurrentRatings, AACommFwInfo.Targets target = Targets.Legacy) Parameters api CommAPI instance of the API class to perform the download connData ConnectionData connection data fwDataFile string full FW file path (.hex/.bin) verFile string full FW version file path (.ver, can be null for MAS02) password string the password for the FW download (contact API provider for more info) verifyCurrentRatings bool specifies whether to verify connected controller currents with HEX file reported currents/> target AACommFwInfo.Targets indicates the target core of the FW (defaults to Legacy) Remarks The instance is marked busy for the whole call, the currents pre-flight included - that pre-flight connects the API and reads from it, so a second call arriving while it runs is refused rather than allowed to drive the same API.

String parameter is the error description Also invoked, with "Async operation in progress!", for a call refused because an operation is already running on this instance; that refusal leaves the running operation and its state untouched. This callback is shared by every call on the instance, so the running operation's handler also receives the refusal text, in no guaranteed order relative to its own result. Also invoked, with "Operation cancelled", when <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.RecData.AACommDataRecManager.CancelUpload" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> ends the running operation. public Action<string> OnError { get; set; } Property Value Action<string> OnForceTrigger Fired when the ForceTrigger(ICommService) completes successfully public Action OnForceTrigger { get; set; } Property Value Action OnRecUploadNextProgress Fired during UploadRecDataNonblocking(ICommService) sequential upload. Cancels a sequential UploadRecDataNonblocking(ICommService) upload, and stops the WaitForRecToEnd(uint, ICommService) poll between queries. Does nothing when no operation is running. The "Operation cancelled" report is made on the calling thread, before this method returns. A request already on the wire is not recalled: a command, a parameter batch, a blocking UploadRecData(ICommService) or a WaitForRecToEnd(uint, ICommService) query in flight still gets its reply. A reply that arrives after the cancel is discarded: it re-arms no poll, sends nothing, runs no completion and releases nothing. In case of incorrect argument, <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.RecData.AACommDataRecManager.OnError" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> is invoked on a new thread Use <xref href="AAComm.Extensions.RecData.AACommDataRecManager.OnUploadRecData" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> event to get the uploaded data public void UploadRecData(ICommService api) Parameters api ICommService CONNECTED instance of CommAPI class UploadRecDataNonblocking(ICommService) Asynchronous function, uploads recorded data using the sequential RecUploadNext protocol. Ethernet only: on any other channel type it throws NotSupportedException. Uses Zynq stream transport when advertised by both peers; otherwise uses legacy bulk messages, or one message per element for a parameter not allowed in bulk. A timeout or disconnect is never retried because part of the array may already have been applied. Every element is checked against the controller's message table first: one whose index or value the table rules out ends the call as Rejected with that element's index and error code, and nothing is sent. A parameter the table refuses outright (unknown, read-only, not an array) throws ArgumentException. The server arms the same budget against the controller and tears the channel down as fatal when it expires, so a stalled download also stalls whatever is queued behind it for every client on that channel. skipUserUnits bool Bypass User Units conversion for this download. Returns ArrayDownloadResult Remarks On ProtocolError with CrcMismatch the controller verifies the payload checksum only after applying every element, so the result reports a full AppliedCount for a write whose integrity check failed. Read the array back rather than trusting that count. Wire format: Firmware-Main docs/features/Array-Stream-Download.md. api/AAComm.Services.ArrayStreamError.htm.summary: Enum ArrayStreamError Namespace AAComm.Services Assembly AAComm.dll Array-stream protocol errors reported by the controller when Status is ProtocolError. The firmware allocates these above the interpreter's range so the two never collide. public enum ArrayStreamError Fields BadCount = 61444 Element count of zero, or above 65535. BadFlags = 61442 A flags bit the controller does not define. BadIndexRange = 61445 First index zero, or a final index above 65535. BadVersion = 61441 Message type or protocol version not understood. BadWidth = 61443 Element width other than 4 or 8. CrcMismatch = 61446 Payload checksum mismatch. Every element was still applied before the check ran. None = 0 No stream-protocol error. api/AAComm.Services.Diagnostics.AACommDe.summary: Class AACommDebugLog Namespace AAComm.Services.Diagnostics Assembly AAComm.dll Process-wide, zero-config, always-on diagnostic log for the AAComm client — the client-side counterpart of AACommServer's debug log. Session-lifecycle events (construction, connect outcomes, sync-timeout expiries, FATALs, disconnects) accumulate in an in-memory ring; healthy steady state does zero file IO. A severe event (sync phase-2 teardown, FATAL, comms error) snapshots the ring to %LocalAppData%\PCSuite\AAComm_DebugLogs{yyyy_MM_dd_HH-mm-ss}{process}{pid}_{trigger}.log off the hot path (debounced, 5 s), because a library in the customer's process has no reliable exit hook to save on. Never per-message traffic — that is the AACommServer comm log's job. Every line is tagged HH:mm:ss.fff [api#N/conn#M] text: api#N identifies the CommAPI instance, conn#M its successive channel opens; the connect line carries the full endpoint (and the socket's local port, which AACommServer's log can join against its per-client UserId). public static class AACommDebugLog Inheritance object AACommDebugLog Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties Sink Optional host bridge: receives each event line as (source, formatted line), where source is the line's identity tag — api#N or api#N/conn#M, and on the connect line the tag also carries →endpoint, so hosts routing on source should prefix-match. The one-time process header line is ring-only and does not reach the sink. Mirrors AACommServer's GlobalLogger.GlobalDebugLog; lets a host forward AAComm diagnostics into its own session log. Invoked synchronously on the logging thread — keep handlers cheap. public static Action<string, string> Sink { get; set; } Property Value Action<string, string> Methods Flush() Writes the current in-memory ring to a timestamped snapshot file NOW (synchronously), without clearing it. Never throws; healthy processes may call this on demand. public static void Flush()

api/AAComm.Services.LockEventWriteOrder..summary: Class LockEventWriteOrder Namespace AAComm.Services Assembly AAComm.dll The write order a parameter restore needs under the lock/event guards of firmware that declares LockEventMode up to 2 (see Mode2Supported(MessageData)). In LockEventMode 1 and 2 that firmware refuses a change to a lock/event dependency while LockEn or EventOn is on (error 403), and refuses LockEn/EventOn after a dependency changed until the offset is recomputed (404; 335 if it was never computed). Per axis, when the rows touch a dependency or LockEventMode, the order becomes: LockEn and EventOn off (both, whether or not the rows carry them: a .par has neither, and either one armed refuses the change), then the other rows in their original order, then LockEventMode, then LockEventInit when the axis is in mode 1 at re-arm, then the rows' own LockEn/EventOn in their order, so the last one requested is the state left. Axes whose rows touch neither keep their rows untouched and in place. The mode at re-arm is the rows' LockEventMode when they carry one, otherwise the controller's current mode (ReadCurrentModes(IList<string>, Func<AACommMessage, AACommEventArgs>)). An AGM800-EC enable forces mode 2 only at the next enable, so an AGM800-EC restored into mode 1 gets the LockEventInit like any other controller. public static class LockEventWriteOrder Inheritance object LockEventWriteOrder Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Fields Dependencies The keywords whose change invalidates the lock/event offset; EncFilt, AuxEncFilt and CurrDir are not among them. The firmware counts AuxEncDir only with the aux source (EncSinCosHWEn=3) and VEncFact/VEncFactDen only with the virtual-encoder source (2); the order treats them as dependencies always, since a row can't tell which source the controller will have when it lands, and disarming first is harmless. public static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> Dependencies Field Value IReadOnlyList<string> EcEnableLockOffsetFault CiA402 0x603F error code an AGM800-EC raises when Enable Operation can't learn the lock/event offset. public const int EcEnableLockOffsetFault = 29440 Field Value int EventOn public const string EventOn = "EventOn" Field Value string LockEn public const string LockEn = "LockEn" Field Value string LockEventInit public const string LockEventInit = "LockEventInit" Field Value string LockEventMode public const string LockEventMode = "LockEventMode" Field Value string Methods EnableForcesMode2(int, MessageData) Whether Enable Operation forces LockEventMode 2 on this controller: an AGM800-EC whose firmware declares LockEventMode up to 2. The AGD EtherCAT drives lock locally and have no lock/event offset. public static bool EnableForcesMode2(int productType, MessageData lockEventMode) Parameters productType int lockEventMode MessageData Returns bool Mode2Supported(MessageData) Whether the connected firmware accepts LockEventMode 2, read from the keyword's declared maximum in the controller's About table (there is no separate support keyword). The 403/404 guards ship in the same firmware, so this is also whether a restore needs Order(IList<string>, Func<string, bool>, Func<char, int?>). public static bool Mode2Supported(MessageData lockEventMode) Parameters lockEventMode MessageData Returns bool Order(IList<string>, Func<string, bool>, Func<char, int?>) Reorders rows (<axis><Mnemonic>=<value>, as a .par holds them). Pure; the caller decides whether the controller has the guards at all (Mode2Supported(MessageData)). public static LockEventWriteOrder.Plan Order(IList<string> rows, Func<string, bool> isSupported = null, Func<char, int?> currentMode = null) Parameters rows IList<string> The rows to order; the result keeps every one of them exactly once. isSupported Func<string, bool> Whether the controller has a keyword (LockEn, EventOn, LockEventInit); an unsupported one is never added. Null means all are. currentMode Func<char, int?> The controller's current LockEventMode for an axis, or null when unknown; consulted only for a touched axis whose rows carry no LockEventMode (see ReadCurrentModes(IList<string>, Func<AACommMessage, AACommEventArgs>)). Returns LockEventWriteOrder.Plan ReadCurrentModes(IList<string>, Func<AACommMessage, AACommEventArgs>) Reads the current LockEventMode (<axis>LockEventMode) of each axis whose rows touch a lock/event dependency but carry no LockEventMode row, for Order(IList<string>, Func<string, bool>, Func<char, int?>)'s currentMode. An axis whose read failed (an error reply, a reply that isn't a number, or a throw) maps to null: without its mode the LockEventInit decision can't be made, so the caller writes nothing. sendReceive is a synchronous send; never call this from a reply callback. public static Dictionary<char, int?> ReadCurrentModes(IList<string> rows, Func<AACommMessage, AACommEventArgs> sendReceive) Parameters rows IList<string> sendReceive Func<AACommMessage, AACommEventArgs> Returns Dictionary<char, int?>

These are written only through the User Units API (ControllerMessagesContainer.TrySetUnitsSync): the units name is a multi-write char array whose adapter cache can't be kept correct by sniffing single raw writes, so raw assignments to them are rejected by the Tx-build gate. The read-only group array (GroupSuffix) and the event-driven enable parameter (UserUnitsEn) are deliberately NOT included. public static bool IsUserUnitsConfig(string mnemonic) Parameters mnemonic string Returns bool MessageAssignsUserUnitsConfig(string) Returns whether a full controller message (single axis prefix + mnemonic + optional [index] + assignment), e.g. "APosUnitFct=0.5" or "BPosUnitUnt[3]=109", assigns a User Units config parameter (see IsUserUnitsConfig(string)). Queries (no '='/',') return false. Provisioning tools use this to decide whether a bulk write needs a post-write CommAPI.RefreshUserUnits to resync the scaling cache the raw write left stale. public static bool MessageAssignsUserUnitsConfig(string message) Parameters message string Returns bool TryParseUserUnitsEnAssignment(string, out char, out bool) Detects a single-axis <xref href="AAComm.Services.UserUnits.UUMnemonics.UserUnitsEn" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> assignment, e.g. "AUserUnitsEn=1" or "BUserUnitsEn,0". Returns false for queries (no '='/',') and for any other mnemonic. Used on the reply path to keep the enabled cache ack-authoritative and to fire the change event. Single-char axis prefix only. Spaces are removed first, matching the way the controller-message parser tokenises: "AUserUnitsEn =1" is a write the controller accepts, so the cache has to see it too. public static bool TryParseUserUnitsEnAssignment(string message, out char axis, out bool enabled) Parameters message string the sent message (axis + mnemonic + assignment) axis char resolved upper-cased axis char when the method returns true enabled bool the assigned state (value != "0") when the method returns true Returns bool

Owner 0 with sub-version 0 is a final release; owner 0 with a sub-version N is release candidate N of the release; a non-zero owner is a development build. Order: by Major.Minor.Patch, then within one release the candidates (by sub-version) before the final, then the development builds (by owner, then sub-version). FloatHelper Central floating-point resolution for hardware-uploaded data. Controller parameters may be transmitted as bit-masked int/long values representing IEEE 754 float/double. This class resolves those raw values to their correct floating-point representation. GlobalVar user program Header Info "Global Variable" description HeaderParser a service class to parse the currently loaded User Program Header data, obtained by inquiring "AProgInfo" LocaleProvider Singleton object that provides localized Error and Status strings Currently supported languages: "en-US", "zh-CN" Use for localized Controller Errors strings LockEventWriteOrder The write order a parameter restore needs under the lock/event guards of firmware that declares LockEventMode up to 2 (see Mode2Supported(MessageData)). In LockEventMode 1 and 2 that firmware refuses a change to a lock/event dependency while LockEn or EventOn is on (error 403), and refuses LockEn/EventOn after a dependency changed until the offset is recomputed (404; 335 if it was never computed). Per axis, when the rows touch a dependency or LockEventMode, the order becomes: LockEn and EventOn off (both, whether or not the rows carry them: a .par has neither, and either one armed refuses the change), then the other rows in their original order, then LockEventMode, then LockEventInit when the axis is in mode 1 at re-arm, then the rows' own LockEn/EventOn in their order, so the last one requested is the state left. Axes whose rows touch neither keep their rows untouched and in place. The mode at re-arm is the rows' LockEventMode when they carry one, otherwise the controller's current mode (ReadCurrentModes(IList, Func)). An AGM800-EC enable forces mode 2 only at the next enable, so an AGM800-EC restored into mode 1 gets the LockEventInit like any other controller. api/AAComm.Shared.ServerCompat.html.summary: Enum ServerCompat Namespace AAComm.Shared Assembly AAComm.dll Classification of the AACommServer this client attached to, reported by after a successful Connect. The version floor CLASSIFIES the attach, it never rejects: a legacy server still connects (compat mode), because a new client must coexist with a server started by an older SDK application on the same machine — but the degraded mode is queryable here instead of silent. public enum ServerCompat Fields Current = 1 Binary server at or above the client's floor — full feature set (correlated reply routing, channel events, version-gated features). LegacyAscii = 3 ASCII-only server: arrival-order reply routing, no channel events. The client's ASCII pipeline is frozen (deprecated) and kept solely for this compat mode. LegacyBinary = 2 Binary server below the floor (or reporting no parseable version): correlated routing works, but features behind newer version gates silently skip. Dormant while the floor equals the typed-payloads shipping version — a pre-typed binary server fails the handshake gate and attaches as ASCII (LegacyAscii); this value becomes reachable again at the next floor raise, for older-but-typed servers. articles/advanced/firmware-download.html.title: Firmware & FPGA Download | Agito AAComm SDK
articles/advanced/firmware-download.html.summary: Firmware & FPGA Download Overview Firmware (and, for non-AGM800 products, FPGA) images download over Ethernet or RS-232 — never CAN (see Transport support). AGM800 binary (.bin) firmware is validated via embedded magic markers and an optional .ver file, at parity with the non-AGM800 (.hex FW + .dat FPGA) products. The surface lives in AAComm/Extensions/: AACommFwInfo validates the file set (ValidateFwFiles) and delegates AGM800 .bin parsing to AACommBinFwInfo, while AACommDownloadFW and AACommDownloadFPGA run the packet loops. Transport support FW download runs over Ethernet (AGM800 family — Ethernet only; an AGM800-EC ESI download also over the firmware-sim Simulation channel) or RS-232. It is NOT supported over CAN — AACommDownloadFW (StartDownloading/StartDownloadingSafe) rejects a CAN ConnectionData up front with "Firmware download is not supported over CAN…". The controller's CAN boot-loader FW-data contract is owned by the C2000 flash kernel at 0x100000 (separate from the application image) and is not met by this client path, so a CAN attempt fails controller-side with ERR 43 (unexpected character) / ERR 15 (unexpected byte count). Use Ethernet or RS-232. The AGD301 FW (.hex) and FPGA (.dat) download paths are HW-validated over RS-232 on both the String and Binary IPC protocols (Agd301HardwareTests, goldens AGD301orAGC301_2D05_V3.0.42.hex + AGD301_for_BissC_and_SinCos_v2.7.2.dat); the FW .hex also flashes over Ethernet (the office rig's AGD301 at 172.1.1.105, by aacomm.cli flash). FPGA download requires normal mode — it rejects BOOT. The complete gate matrix per download path — product, transport, exact-address and subnet rules, boot mode, file targets, version compatibility — with the CI-rig consequences is docs/ci-cd/fw-fpga-download-constraints.md. Download paths AACommDownloadFW picks its path from the connection's product and the target the caller passes: Connection Target Path File AGM400, AGM800, Pulse-Sync, AGM800-EC Legacy DownloadFW_MAS02: 700-byte MAS02 packets .bin firmware AGM800-EC EC_ESI DownloadFW: DownloadESI, then the image as Intel-HEX lines .bin SII image AGD101-EC, AGD155-EC, AGD156-EC EC_MCU1 / EC_CM / EC_ESI DownloadFW: DownloadFW / DownloadCM / DownloadESI, then Intel-HEX lines .hex; .bin ESI image for EC_ESI legacy products Legacy DownloadFW: DownloadFW, then the .hex lines .hex An AGM800-EC SII image and an AGM800-EC firmware image are both .bin files, so the target is the caller's to assert — AAComm never infers ESI from the file, but refuses an EC_ESI file larger than the 16 KiB an ESI image can address, or one that carries firmware identity markers — an SII image does neither. The ESI download runs on the controller's firmware without a boot jump, and connects in full so the controller's own keyword table resolves DownloadESI. An AGM400, AGM800 or Pulse-Sync connection asked for EC_ESI is refused before anything is sent. Every gate per path is in docs/ci-cd/fw-fpga-download-constraints.md. Remote FPGA identity checks AACommDownloadFPGARemote downloads a remote .rpd over the AGM800 family's Ethernet connection, including AGM800-EC. AACommRemoteFpgaInfo reads the adjacent seven-line .ver in this order: FPGA Version, FPGA Size, Remote Type, Remote SubType, Remote Variant, Amplifier Version, Comm Version. The metadata is not a payload checksum. For AGA155 (type 1, subtype 0x0150), compact Remote Variant codes 0x3, 0x6, and 0xA identify 2A03, 2A06, and 2A10 and match CIIdentity[23]. Amplifier Version codes 0x1, 0x2, and 0x3 identify hardware Variant37, Variant47, and Variant46 and match CIIdentity[21]. Comm Version is NA; 8K maps to identity size 2. Marketing strings such as 2A06 are parsed as hexadecimal values, never normalized to the compact codes: select matching compact metadata with compact-identity images. Normal downloads reject known identity mismatches. For controlled engineering comparisons only, set AACommRemoteFpgaInfo.AllowAga155CurrentRatingMismatch = true to permit current code 6 to 10 or 10 to 6 on a matching AGA155 target. It defaults to false and preserves type, subtype, FPGA size, hardware revision, and communication revision checks. It neither permits current code 3 mismatches nor grants an unknown identity override. AllowForce retains its separate unknown (0/NA) semantics; it does not bypass known mismatches. Both options together preserve the other guards. Firmware that does not expose index 23 retains the legacy download path, without variant validation; enabling the option does not prove that validation occurred. Remote image transitions The remote download verifies fresh dual-configuration MSM_CS state: boot (3 or 4) before erase/data writes, and primary (2 or 5) before reporting success. Transition preparation, reconnect acknowledgements and state-read transactions are checked; a successful CIConnect or cached identity alone is insufficient. Only an exact ERR 151 reply to the final reconfiguration trigger, after successful preparation, is treated as uncertain completion. OnStatus retains the original command/error context, then the service makes one reconnect attempt after its image-start delay and reads the requested image state. Failed or malformed replies, an unconnected target or a wrong image terminate the download. Ordinary offline/flash errors and other trigger errors remain terminal. Erase and data transfer are never automatically repeated. The existing file, identity, force/current-rating, exclusive channel and per-axis access guards apply throughout; the local FPGA path and generic low-level CIConnect contract are unchanged. Backward Compatibility No .ver file: AGM800 firmware download proceeds without validation, except that an identity-marked image whose product differs from the connection's, when either one is AGM800-EC, is refused .ver file exists: Performs MD5 checksum, version, and product type validation before download Binary Firmware Parsing (AACommBinFwInfo) Parses Zynq binary firmware files to extract identity and version information using magic markers embedded in the binary. Magic Markers Each marker starts with the signature "AKRB" followed by a type tag: Marker Tag Payload Identity IDNT version(4) + size(4) + int32[32] (128 bytes) Version VERS version(4) + size(4) + char[4][64] (256 bytes) Byte-order note: Marker types are stored as little-endian 32-bit integers. "IDNT" (0x49444E54) appears as bytes 54 4E 44 49 ("TNDI" in a hex editor). Similarly, "VERS" appears as "SREV". Extracted Identity Data (32 int32 values) Index Field 0 Data version 1 Product type 2-6 FW version: Major.Minor.Patch.Owner-Subversion 7 Continuous current limit 8 Peak current limit 9 Number of axes 17 Full scale current 31 Magic end marker (0x12345678) .ver File Format (AGM800) Line 1: Version (optional) e.g. "3.8.0.0-123" Line 2: MD5 (optional) e.g. "MD5:XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX" Line 3: Type (optional) e.g. "Type:AGM800" Valid Type values (prefix match, case-insensitive) depend on the connected product: Connection Accepted Type: Refused AGM800-EC (16) AGM800-EC everything else AGM400 (6), AGM800 (10), PULSE_SYNC (15) AGM800, CiG1-MAS02, MAS02 everything else, AGM800-EC included AGM800-EC is its own image family: its image and the AGM800 image are not interchangeable, although both are .bin files of the same format. Validation Steps (when .ver file exists) MD5 checksum verification (if MD5: line present) Version match between .ver and binary identity data (if binary contains identity markers) Product type validation — two independent checks: Binary identity (if the binary contains identity markers): product-type IDs 6=AGM400, 10=AGM800 and 15=PULSE_SYNC share one image and are considered compatible, checked when the .ver has a version line; 16=AGM800-EC matches only itself, checked with or without a .ver Type string (if a Type: line is present): only the values the table above lists for the connected product are accepted. Note: Pulse-Sync is NOT a valid Type string even though product type 15 passes the binary identity check MAS02 Hex-Encoding (IPC Framing Fix) MAS02 binary FW packets are raw binary that may contain 0x3E 0x0D — the IPC envelope terminator (>\r). To keep the IPC body ASCII-safe, the client wraps each binary chunk with the @#HEX: sigil (CommCommons.HexEncodedPrefix): <message-type-prefix>@#HEX:<hex-pairs>\r The server-side SocketMessageData detects the sigil via IndexOf, strips it, decodes the hex pairs back to raw bytes, and forwards a byte-identical payload to the controller. The per-packet MAS02 header and EOF marker are encoded as hex ASCII strings ("0000" / "FFFF") rather than raw char constants. This @#HEX: framing is the string-protocol path. Under the default binary (protobuf) IPC the raw FW bytes ride in IpcRequest.PayloadBytes with no hex round-trip — see architecture.md (IPC Framing). Post-Reset Disconnect Tolerance Both FW and FPGA download use ResetReplyHelper.IsExpectedPostResetDisconnect after the final packet/batch to handle the race where the controller resets before the OK reply arrives. Disconnect-style replies (ERR 4021, ERR 4020, ERR 4025, channel-fatal) are accepted as success for the last step.

articles/architecture/diagnostics.html.title: Diagnostic Debug Logs | Agito AAComm SDK
articles/architecture/diagnostics.html.summary: Diagnostic Debug Logs — client, server, and how they join The SDK's always-on diagnostic layer: what the AAComm client and AACommServer record about session lifecycle, where the files land, and the procedure that correlates the two logs for a single connection. This is the spec for the diagnostic logs only — the AACommServer comm log (per-channel message traffic, saved from the server UI) and PCSuite's Serilog session log (the PCSuite_DebugLogs sibling) are separate facilities. Design constraints Zero-config, always-on. AAComm runs inside customer processes; a diagnostic that must be enabled first never exists when the incident happens. Zero steady-state file IO. Entries accumulate in an in-memory ring; a healthy process never touches the disk. Only a severe event (or an explicit flush) writes a file. No per-message traffic. Message-level logging is the AACommServer comm log's job; the SendReceive/Send hot paths gain no logging on the success path. No wire change. The client↔server correlation works purely from what each side already sees on its own socket. Folder layout One folder per producer, all under %LocalAppData%\PCSuite\: Folder Producer Written when AAComm_DebugLogs\ AAComm client (AACommDebugLog) severe event or Flush() AACommServer_DebugLogs\ AACommServer (GlobalLogger); sniffer captures under Sniffer\ shutdown save, flush verb, implicit-shutdown save PCSuite_DebugLogs\ PCSuite exes (Serilog session log) continuously (buffered) All debug-log folders prune independently on a file-count cap of 200; when a save finds the folder over the cap, the oldest files are deleted down to the newest 100 (half the cap), so the prune fires rarely rather than on every save. Local application data — not Documents — is deliberate: Documents redirects to OneDrive, whose sync locks capture files and contends with snapshot IO under connect/close churn. Client log — AAComm.Services.Diagnostics.AACommDebugLog Static, process-wide, shared by every CommAPI instance in the process. Line format and identity tags HH:mm:ss.fff [api#N/conn#M] text api#N — the CommAPI instance, numbered in construction order (assigned in the designated constructor every overload funnels into). conn#M — that instance's successive successful channel opens. Before the first open the tag is just api#N. The connect line is the one line whose tag also carries the endpoint: [api#1/conn#1→Ethernet 172.1.1.101:5000]. Every later line is tag-only, so a reader greps the endpoint once and then follows the short tag. The ring's first entry is a one-time header: === AAComm diagnostic log — process <name> (PID <pid>), path <exe path>, AAComm <version>, started <timestamp> === Recorded events Event Line (shape) Construction CommAPI constructed Channel open (per successful open, incl. test opens) channel open (local 127.0.0.1:54321), ServerCompat=Current — the tag carries the endpoint; local is the client→AACS socket's local end, the join key (see below) TestConnection / Connect / ConnectSilent outcome Connect(Ethernet 172.1.1.101:5000) → Success in 812 ms, ServerCompat=Current — result, elapsed, endpoint, and the compat the attempt classified (captured before teardown can reset it; TestConnection always tears down before this line is written) Sync phase-1 expiry (queue abandon, no teardown) sync phase-1 expiry: abandoned in queue after 203 ms (queued-behind-live budget, TimeoutMs=100): "APos" — the budget branch is queued-behind-live (TimeoutMs + 100) or idle+starvation (TimeoutMs + 5000) Sync phase-2 expiry (teardown) sync phase-2 expiry: no reply 402 ms after dispatch at 14:03:07.101 (budget TimeoutMs 100 + 100 + grace 200 = 400 ms): "APos" → teardown — message text truncated to 64 chars. This line is what discriminates phase-1 vs phase-2 in the field Server FATAL frame received server FATAL received: <content> (ASCII and binary pipelines both) Any comms error / FATAL reaching teardown comms error/FATAL: <message> → teardown (the funnel — covers socket death paths that never produce a FATAL frame) Disconnect disconnect (<reason>) — explicit, sync-timeout, fatal, close-server, test-connection complete, or connect failed: <ConnectResult> Flush-on-severity A library in the customer's process has no reliable exit hook, so severity is the flush trigger. Ring: 10 000 entries, oldest 10 % evicted on overflow. Triggers: sync phase-2 teardown (SyncTimeout), FATAL / comms error (Fatal), and the public on-demand AACommDebugLog.Flush() (Flush, synchronous). File: {yyyy_MM_dd_HH-mm-ss}_{process}_{pid}_{trigger}.log — a snapshot of the ring, which is not cleared, so successive snapshots overlap and logging continues. Off the hot path: severity snapshots are written on the ThreadPool; the file path (directory included) is resolved at trigger time, so a concurrent directory change cannot redirect the write or its prune. Debounce: 5 s — multiple severe events inside the window produce one file (a phase-2 teardown and the FATAL it provokes do not double-write). Host bridge — AACommDebugLog.Sink Action<string, string> (source, formatted line): every event line is mirrored to it synchronously, source = the line's identity tag (the connect line's tag carries →endpoint, so hosts routing on source should prefix-match; the one-time header is ring-only). Mirrors GlobalLogger.GlobalDebugLog on the server side; hosts use it to fold AAComm diagnostics into their own session log. Sink and Flush() are the only public surface. Server log — AACommServerCore.GlobalLogger Same mechanics (the ring/file core is one source file, owned by AAComm and compiled into AACommServerCore as a linked source — separate assemblies, separate state, so a chatty client can never evict server entries), different policy: Line format: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss [Debug|Fault|UnhandledException] <source> : <message>. Files in AACommServer_DebugLogs\: {stamp}_Debug.log (the once-on-shutdown save), {stamp}_Flush.log (on-demand snapshot — the client's fire-and-forget CommAPI.FlushDebugLog() verb or the server UI), {stamp}_ImplicitShutdown.log (the abnormal last-client-death save). GlobalDebugLog feeds the server UI's live debug list; LogDebug lines land in both the UI list and the ring. Joining the two logs AACommServer identifies clients only by UserId; the client never learns its UserId. The join key is the client→AACS TCP socket, which both sides see from opposite ends: Client side — the connect line logs the socket's local end: 14:02:59.310 [api#1/conn#1→Ethernet 172.1.1.101:5000] channel open (local 127.0.0.1:54321), ServerCompat=Current Server side — on every client Open, one debug line binds UserId to the socket's remote end (the same address:port): 2026-08-24 14:02:59 [Debug] OnAACommRequest() UserId=7 : Open request for 'ET_172.1.1.101' from client endpoint 127.0.0.1:54321 Procedure, starting from either side: In the client snapshot, find the channel open line for the session of interest → take the local endpoint (127.0.0.1:54321). Grep the server's debug log for that endpoint → the line names the UserId (7). Filter the server log by UserId=7 — every server-side event for that client (malformed frames, tx overflow, implicit-shutdown bookkeeping) now correlates with the client's api#N/conn#M timeline. The reverse direction starts from a UserId and greps the endpoint in the client snapshots. Caveats: ephemeral ports are unique per live connection but recycle over time — on long-uptime machines disambiguate by timestamp proximity; each reconnect is a new conn#M and a new local port, so the join is per-connection, not per-process. Worked example — attributing a sync-timeout teardown The failure this layer exists for: an application reports "AAComm disconnected", the server log shows only an unexplained client close. With the snapshots: 14:03:06.694 [api#1/conn#1] sync phase-2 expiry: no reply 402 ms after dispatch at 14:03:06.291 (budget TimeoutMs 100 + 100 + grace 200 = 400 ms): "APos" → teardown 14:03:06.697 [api#1/conn#1] disconnect (sync-timeout) tells support: the message reached the wire (phase 2, not a queue abandon), the full grace was spent, the client — not the controller protocol — initiated the close, and the {...}_SyncTimeout.log filename alone already names the trigger. The join procedure then locates the same seconds in the server log under the bound UserId to see what the server observed (e.g. queueing behind another client's long operation). Known limitations The header's process path is best-effort (Process.MainModule can be inaccessible under permission/bitness constraints; the header then says unknown). The client ring is process-global: snapshots interleave all CommAPI instances (that is what the api#N tag is for). File IO failures are silently swallowed on the client (a diagnostic must never take the host down); the server side falls back to the Windows Event Log as before. The local-port half of the join key is available only from the real socket-backed transports; test doubles log the connect line without it.

articles/architecture/floating-point.htm.title: Floating Point Resolution | Agito AAComm SDK
articles/architecture/floating-point.htm.summary: AAComm Floating-Point Resolution Principle Data that leaves AAComm via the Extension classes (e.g., RecordingDataContainer, LoggerDataContainer, ScopeDataContainer, AllStatInterpreter) is properly resolved and ready to use. Raw IEEE 754 bit-pattern resolution is handled transparently by these classes. Limitation: Resolution only applies when data is obtained through the Extension mechanism, or for protocols that have Rx-path resolution (see below). If an unsupported upload command is issued directly via CommAPI.Send() — such as from PCSuite Terminal — the raw response is not resolved. The consumer receives unprocessed bit-masked values. The SDK exposes ConFltSnapVal and ProgSnapVal as raw values only and does not resolve them: their source parameters (ConFltSnapSrc / ProgSnapSrc) are user-configurable, so the slot types are known only after the CCC sources are read, and that read-and-resolve step belongs to the caller (PCSuite's FaultDataView and UpSnapshotDecode do it). Number text Every value crosses the AAComm boundary as text — AACommEventArgs carries a reply only as MsgReceived — so each read is a format-then-reparse round trip. Both halves are pinned to CultureInfo.InvariantCulture: '.' as the decimal separator, never a group separator, matching the controller's own ASCII protocol. Formatting. Every floating-point value AAComm emits as text goes through WireNumber.ToWire (AAComm.Internal.Wire): scaled replies and ParamAbout bounds from FloatHelper, the resolved AllStat values in AllStatInterpreter, the User Units factor written by TrySetUnitsSync, the recording-trigger download commands in TriggerContainer. It picks the shortest fixed-precision invariant form that parses back to the same value — G15 else G17 for double, G7 else G9 for float — so two guarantees hold by construction: the text round-trips to the identical value (checked per value, not assumed), and it is byte-identical on every target framework, because every target runs that same selection over specifiers that are themselves target-stable. Neither holds for "R", which is shortest-round-trippable on .NET 8/10, a documented round-trip hazard on 64-bit .NET Framework, and disagrees between the two for 16-significant-digit values; a bare ToString() is worse still — 15-digit lossy on .NET Framework 4.8. Integral wire tokens and the legacy FirmwareVersionStr/FPGAVersionStr are likewise rendered with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, so a negative value never carries the U+2212 minus sign that ICU uses for sv-SE, fi-FI, nb-NO, et-EE and lt-LT — the reply text is truncated to bytes one char at a time, which would turn -12345 into \x1212345. Parsing. Where AAComm parses a controller-supplied decimal number it uses an explicit NumberStyles.Float | NumberStyles.AllowThousands and the invariant culture: the assignment value in CanMessageParser, the factor read back in UserUnitGroup, the About-data bounds in MessageData, and the values AllStatInterpreter decodes. The transmit seam in PayloadBuilder is the one deliberate exception: it reads the outgoing assignment with plain NumberStyles.Float, no AllowThousands, because a , is an assignment separator in the controller's own grammar — reading 1,5 as one thousand five hundred there would rewrite a command the parser rejects into one it accepts. Consumers must do the same. A reply reaches the caller as text; parsing it in the current culture reads an invariant 0.01 as 1 on a comma-decimal locale, or throws. Resolution Core logic lives in FloatHelper (AAComm.Services) — public static class, callable directly by all consumers. FloatHelper.ResolveFloatingPoint(MessageData md, long val, bool doubleSupported, bool floatSupport) determines the correct conversion based on the parameter's MessageData type: float/double with doubleSupported — LongToDouble() (64-bit IEEE 754) float with !doubleSupported and floatSupport — IntToFloat() (32-bit IEEE 754) float with !doubleSupported and !floatSupport — returned as-is (float hole protection) int / long — returned as-is null metadata (unknown parameter) — returned as-is (safe fallback) FloatHelper.ResolveFromCCC(int ccc, long rawVal, IMessagesContainer dataContainer, bool doubleSupported, bool floatSupport) resolves via Complex CAN Code: parses CCC -> looks up MessageData -> delegates to ResolveFloatingPoint. Throws FormatException on NaN or Infinity. Float Hole Protection AllStat_64bit protocols (AllStat, Logger, Scope, ConFltSnap, ProgSnap) never transmit 32-bit float bit patterns. They either send raw integers or 64-bit doubles. These protocols pass floatSupport: false, which blocks the IntToFloat path and prevents garbage values when doubleSupported=false and a parameter has float metadata. RecUpload and ParamAbout pass floatSupport: true. Firmware-Side UserUnits (Recording Header) The per-vector UserUnits integer stored in the recording header (VectorDataContainer.UserUnits, read from GetUserUnitsIndex(i)) is part of a parallel firmware-level scaling system. It is mutually exclusive with the PCSuite UU feature at the firmware level. This value is preserved as metadata in RecParamHeader and AGF files but is NOT used for PCSuite UU scaling. PCSuite UU factors are looked up dynamically through the centralized FloatHelper.ResolveUserUnitsFactor() — CommAPI.GetUserUnitsEnabled() + ControllerMessagesContainer.TryGetUserUnitAxis(), plus the per-message AACommMessage.SkipUserUnits opt-out — which FloatHelper.ApplyUserUnits() wraps for the callers that only need to multiply. User Units: Embedded vs Global Firmware declares two independent user-units systems. They are one declaration each of two different things, not two declarations of one — different membership between them is by design. System Declared by Who converts Embedded the bInUserUnits field of each keyword's KW_ROW attribute row — USER_UNITS / AUX_USER_UNITS / PD_USER_UNITS / SCALING / NO_USER_UNITS / FUNC_UNITS (Firmware-Main:CommonC/AG300_CTL01Params.c) the controller, on the comm path, by the per-axis UsrUnits / AuxUsrUnits / PDUsrUnits ratio — live values reach AAComm already converted; the About table and ParamAbout report a SCALING parameter's bounds raw, in the controller's internal unit, and MessageData / FloatHelper.ResolveParamAbout divide them by ScalingFact once Global the gl*UnitGroup[] CAN-code arrays (Firmware-Main:CommonC/AG300_CTL01UtilityFuncs.c) AAComm, on the Tx and Rx paths, from the group membership and per-axis factor it reads at connect For the SDK the group arrays are authoritative. UserUnitsAdapter.RefreshSync reads the UnitGrp[] membership arrays, the UnitFct factor and the UnitUnt[] unit names, and nothing else. The keyword flag describes controller behaviour and is not an AAComm input — deriving a parameter's AAComm units contract from it gives the wrong answer. The two sets differ (one firmware revision flags 92 KW_ROW rows for the embedded system while the eight group arrays hold 80 CAN codes between them) and they move independently, so treat the counts as an illustration, never as a number to rely on. The systems are mutually exclusive per parameter and firmware enforces it: CheckGlobalUserUnitsConflict (Firmware-Main:CommonC/AG300_CTL01Interpreter.c) rejects an assign or a read with error 338, GLOBAL_VS_EMBEDDED_USERUNITS_CONFLICT, when the keyword is flagged for the embedded system, its embedded ratio is non-default, its CAN code is in the Global group array matching that flag, and UserUnitsEn is set for that axis. EtherCAT controllers implement the embedded system only: Firmware-Ethercat:Source/Params.c declares the embedded flags and the UsrUnits / AuxUsrUnits / PDUsrUnits parameters, but no UserUnitsEn, no group arrays and no factor parameters. RefreshSync bails with UUErrors.NoUserUnits and the Global layer never engages. PCSuite's view of the Global system, group by group: PCSuite/Core/Configuration/UserUnits/user-units.md. User Units Transmit Seam PayloadBuilder applies the Global system on the way out, above the transport branch — the same step in BuildPayload (string IPC) and BuildTypedPayload (binary IPC), run before either asks which channel it is on. An assignment is divided by the factor of its own parameter (FloatHelper.ResolveUserUnitsFactor, the lookup the receive path uses) and re-rendered with WireNumber.ToWire; the API-only config gate (*UnitFct / *UnitUnt[], error 4023, bypassed per message by AACommMessage.AllowUserUnitsConfig) rejects there too. CanMessageParser reads the assignment as-is — the text reaching it is already in controller units. The seam resolves the command from a copy with every space removed — the tokenisation CanMessageParser itself uses, so APos =1.5 is the same write as APos=1.5 and meets the same gate and the same factor. A command it rewrites crosses in that normalised form; one it does not rewrite crosses byte-for-byte as the caller wrote it. A command the seam cannot resolve — a query, an unknown mnemonic — crosses untouched: the CCC builder owns its error (MnemonicNotFound for an unknown one), and on the bare-ASCII transports there is no error to raise. Two rules follow from where the gate sits: An assignment to a User Units config parameter is rejected 4023 before the value is validated. A malformed, out-of-range or wrong-form value on a real *UnitFct / *UnitUnt[] reports 4023 rather than the parser's 8/9/14/25 — the gate must not depend on a validation the bare-ASCII transports never run. A value the seam cannot read as a finite number (1e400, Infinity, NaN, 1,5) is left exactly as written for the CCC builder to judge, never rendered onto the wire in a rewritten form. An assignment to a firmware-integral parameter (ParamType 0 or 3 — MessageData.IsInt / IsLong) crosses as an integer, rounded to-even in controller counts, on every transport. The rounding belongs here, below the division: rounding a display value above the seam rounds in the wrong space (at a 0.01 mm/count factor it quantises to 100 counts, not 1). CanMessageParser already rounds that way when it packs a CCC frame, so the seam only closes the gap the string transports leave — 244.39 / 0.01 is 24438.999999999996, which used to reach an RS-232 controller as that text while the same command inside a CCC frame carried 24439. The rule applies at factor 1 too, because the caller's value is a display value and may carry a fraction the firmware cannot hold. Float and double parameters keep their fraction, and a value that is already integral is not a rewrite — the command crosses with its original bytes. What a message type does is an explicit table, not a consequence of which branch reaches the CCC builder: Message type Transmit User Units Regular, ResetRequest, EraseUserProg, Continuous scaled once, above the transport branch EthernetASCII scaled once for the single-command key (A), after the key char is set aside; the ASCII-bulk keys (L, I) carry a ;-joined list this seam does not parse and cross raw BulkMessage, BulkMessageIgnore scaled per sub-message inside the bulk segment loop, so a rejected segment keeps the halt-on-error / ADoNothing semantics Firmware, UserProgram, UserProgramBin, SpecialBulk, SpecialBulkB, BulkMessageCNC, BulkMessageCNCB, InternalAACS raw in both directions — scaling a download payload corrupts it The recording download opts out per message: AACommDataRecManager sends its parameter batch with skipUserUnits: true, because TriggerContainer's Tx constructor has already de-scaled RecTrigVal / RecTrigValMax and a second pass would square the factor. User Units Cache Lifetime The Global User-Units factors are read from the controller and cached in ControllerMessagesContainer.UserUnits. The cache is populated by CommAPI.Connect, cleared by Disconnect, and re-read after a controller reboot the session survives — a completed MessageType.ResetRequest, sync or async (Session.SendReceive / Session.RunUserCallback). A reset that came back an error leaves the cached values in place; a re-read that cannot reach the controller clears them rather than leaving the pre-reset factors behind. The firmware / FPGA download EOF steps also reboot the controller, but those flows end in CommAPI.Disconnect, which clears the cache on the way out. A refresh rebuilds the configuration off to the side and publishes it in one swap, so a reply being scaled on the receiver thread meanwhile resolves against the complete old configuration or the complete new one — never a half-filled cache. A raw write to *UnitFct / *UnitUnt that bypasses the config gate (AACommMessage.AllowUserUnitsConfig) does not update the cache — provisioning tools resync it with CommAPI.RefreshUserUnits(). Double Support Flags Two independent flags control double support for different protocol groups: Flag Source Protocols Features_01.DoublePhase_1_Supported Identity[26] bit 28 RecUpload Features_02.AllStat_64bit_Supported Identity[62] bit 3 AllStat, LoggerUpload, ScopeUpload, ParamAbout, ConFltSnapVal, ProgSnapVal Protocols Protocol Container doubleSupported floatSupport Auto-resolved Rx-path resolved UU-scaled RecUpload RecordingDataContainer DoublePhase_1_Supported true Yes No Yes (ApplyUserUnits in ReadRecParamsData) LoggerUpload LoggerDataContainer AllStat_64bit_Supported false Yes No Yes (via PacketDataParser) ScopeUpload ScopeDataContainer AllStat_64bit_Supported false Yes No Yes (via PacketDataParser) AllStat AllStatInterpreter AllStat_64bit_Supported false Yes Yes Yes (Resolve, per value's own parameter) ParamAbout FloatHelper.ResolveParamAbout AllStat_64bit_Supported true Yes (inline) Yes Yes (factor of the queried parameter, not of ParamAbout) ConFltSnapVal PCSuite FaultDataView AllStat_64bit_Supported false No (PCSuite UI) No Yes (PCSuite FaultDataView) ProgSnapVal PCSuite UpSnapshotDecode AllStat_64bit_Supported false No (PCSuite UI) No Yes (PCSuite UpSnapshotDecode) LoggerUpload / ScopeUpload Both use PacketDataParser for the common wire format: nPackets, [header, val1, val2, ...], ..., 0. Header is packet ID (Logger) or Time (Scope). Resolution is applied per value using the caller-provided MessageData list. PCSuite adapts these containers into its UI models. The CSV import path in LoggerData bypasses AAComm resolution (values are already resolved in the file). AllStat AllStatInterpreter requires a connected CommAPI (constructor delegates validation to RecParamsResolver.ValidateAPI). Every field in AllStatAxisData is resolved via mnemonic lookup against the controller's MessagesContainer — float/double fields get bit-pattern conversion, integer fields pass through as double. Rx-Path Resolution (ConvertReplyToFloatIfNeed) FloatHelper.ConvertReplyToFloatIfNeed is the inline Rx-path resolver for all message replies. It intercepts raw controller replies before delivery to the caller and converts IEEE 754 bit patterns to floating-point values. This ensures that even low-level SendReceive() consumers (e.g., PCSuite Terminal) receive properly resolved data. Resolved in the Rx path: Single-value parameters: float (IntToFloat) and double (LongToDouble) based on MessageData type. Note: the single-value path dispatches purely on MessageData.IsFloat/IsDouble — it does NOT check the doubleSupported/floatSupport flags. An unscaled float parameter is rendered by WireNumber.ToWire(float), in its own width: the reply carries at most 9 significant digits and re-parses to the bit pattern the controller holds, where the widened double form of 1e-9f is 9.9999997171806854E-10 — below that parameter's own declared minimum, and rejected on the way back down. A scaled float value (User Units factor other than 1) is a genuine double and is rendered as one: narrowing the product would cost the ulp that carries the transmit-side division back to the stored float32. ParamAbout: multi-value State,MIN,MAX,DEFAULT — delegated to FloatHelper.ResolveParamAbout AllStat: multi-value comma-separated longs per axis/group — delegated to AllStatInterpreter.ResolveRawReply. Uses the static mnemonic arrays and the private Resolve() instance method to convert each value in group order. Bit-pattern conversion runs only when AllStat_64bit_Supported; User Units scaling is applied either way, matching the structured ParseAllStatData path. NOT resolved in the Rx path (CAN code unknown at Rx flow time): RecUpload: not resolved here — RecordingDataContainer parses raw longs and resolves per-vector with the correct feature flags. Rx-path resolution would double-convert (long→string→long parse failure) RecUploadNext: sequential packet protocol — the CAN codes are not embedded in the N2 data packets ScopeUpload / LoggerUpload: the CAN codes are supplied by the caller, not present in the reply ConFltSnapVal / ProgSnapVal: raw values only; the source CCCs are user-configurable, and resolving against them is the caller's work Error Handling AAComm throws generic FormatException on invalid floating-point values (NaN, Infinity). Consumer applications (e.g., PCSuite) catch and localize these messages.

articles/architecture/pipeline.html.title: Architecture Overview | Agito AAComm SDK
articles/architecture/pipeline.html.summary:
AAComm Architecture Client-side communication library for sending commands to hardware controllers via AACommServer. Architecture Overview AAComm is a client library that provides a high-level API for user applications to communicate with hardware controllers. It manages the connection to AACommServer, queues messages, handles responses, and maintains controller state information. Communication Pipeline The default wire protocol is binary: new CommAPI() constructs a BinaryCommHandler with negotiation enabled, so every connect opens binary-first. The ASCII pipeline (CommHandler) is deprecated and reached only as a connect-time fallback against a server that cannot speak the typed-payload binary dialect. Both sit behind the same ICommHandler seam, so the queueing, routing and callback machinery below is identical on either path; the protocol-layer differences are called out where they exist. CommAPI.Protocol reports which one a live session negotiated. Note: Send and SendReceive use independent FIFO pipelines sharing a single underlying wire. Each path has its own queue (Channel), its own dispatcher task, and its own in-flight slot. Ordinary messages in the two flows do not gate each other — a long-running async Send callback does not block a concurrent SendReceive, and a SendReceive parked on its safety-net wait does not block subsequent Sends. Async Reset is the deliberate exception: later dispatch is parked until reset recovery completes. Per-flow FIFO is preserved (consecutive Sends fire callbacks in order; consecutive SRs return in order); cross-flow ordering is NOT guaranteed (an async Send and a sync SendReceive issued back-to-back may dispatch in either order). Wire writes from the two dispatchers are serialized by an internal mutex, and each dispatched message is stamped with a session-scoped correlation id (copied onto IpcRequest by the binary handler; the ASCII handler ignores it). On the binary protocol the server echoes the id on the routed reply and the receiver routes by identity (Session.TryTakeInFlight); an id of 0 — the string protocol or a legacy binary server — falls back to wire-arrival-order routing via the _wireOrder queue (safe because AACommServer processes one message per channel at a time, answers server-internal IA: queries through the same per-channel FIFO, and each client socket has a single ordered writer — so replies arrive in send order). For replies, the receiver thread hands the parsed args to the originating flow's dispatcher via a per-iteration TaskCompletionSource, and the dispatcher runs the user callback on its own thread — the receiver thread does not invoke OnReplyReceived. For push messages, the receiver hands the parsed payload to the OnPushMessageReceived event via Task.Run, so user code runs on the ThreadPool, not the receiver thread. The one exception is OnCommsError: it is invoked synchronously on the receiver thread, and long-running work in that handler will stall reply / push classification until it returns (after a fatal the session is being torn down anyway, but handlers that need to dispatch onto a UI thread should off-load with Task.Run). This receiver-never-blocks-on- reply-callbacks discipline is what unblocks the bug where an async Send callback parked on a UI dispatcher would deadlock a concurrent SendReceive from the UI thread. SendReceive is implemented on top of the sync pipeline: it builds a tagged duplicate of the user's message (IsSyncRequest = true), installs an internal wait-handle hook as OnReplyReceived, and blocks until the reply arrives or the safety-net timeout expires. The per-message IsSyncRequest marker drives event-suppression (OnCommsError and the long-operation events OnLongOperationStarted/OnLongOperationEnded are not raised for sync requests; the Reset recovery sleep is skipped). graph TB subgraph "User Application" App[Application Code] end subgraph "AAComm Library" subgraph "Public API Layer" API[CommAPI
